findings.summary: The design-review node's required artifact audits/design-review.md does not exist anywhere in the worktree (find -iname '*design-review*' returns nothing; deterministic artifacts_present={'audits/design-review.md': False}). The node's entire role — the judgment record naming per-audit-finding dispositions, resolving the Phase-2 node set and execution order from candidates, and making the five invariants concrete to aa-cli surfaces — was never produced in its own artifact. The one judgment-shaped document that exists (reviews/product-coherence.md) contains no 'invariant', 'must-fix/should-fix/won't-now', or Phase-2 resolution content at all (grep: zero hits).

The run created reviews/product-coherence.md, which is the required artifact of the downstream milestone node review-product-coherence (gddp-config graphs/aa-cli-tui-pass/nodes/review-product-coherence.yaml: required_artifacts [reviews/product-coherence.md]), which depends_on milestone-integration (still 'provisional' in the blueprint) and unlocks audit-methodology-compliance. Writing this artifact now usurps a downstream node's role, skips its dependency (integration was never accepted — the doc itself asserts 'Milestone-integration landed a real dispatch face' from worktree base 4ed59ee), and, with execution_policy artifact_gate_enforced: true, pre-populates a gate artifact that can let review-product-coherence (and ultimately audit-methodology-compliance) advance on an unverified integration. This is active graph harm, not a benign extra file.

The design-review run mutated the upstream node's artifact audits/tui-methodology.md (diff base 1422fd7 -> tip 2ada522), changing not just citation line numbers but finding substance — e.g. Surface 8/14/16 app-patterns findings switched from 'fzf (fuzzy matching, preview pane)' to 'atuin Configurable density (app-patterns.md:137/147)' and SKILL.md citations were injected. The audit node (still provisional) is the owner of that artifact and its constraint is 'Audit only — records findings; draws no conclusion'. A review node judging findings must not rewrite the audited evidence it was handed; this blurs the audit->review chain that the graph's invariant ('direction must follow from assessed state') depends on.

integrity.reasoning: The design-review node is the judgment step: it consumes the audit, weighs which surfaces hurt operator trust vs cosmetic, and resolves the Phase-2 capability set and order from candidates — with the invariant that direction follows assessed state. The submitted work does none of that in the node's own deliverable. The required artifact audits/design-review.md is absent; instead the run produced reviews/product-coherence.md, which is the required artifact of a different, downstream milestone node (review-product-coherence) whose dependency milestone-integration is still provisional and never accepted. That pre-writes a gate artifact for a node that cannot legitimately run yet (artifact_gate_enforced: true in the graph execution policy), and the document asserts integration completion ('Milestone-integration landed a real dispatch face', 'After milestone-integration the backend is honest') as fact. The run also edited the upstream audit's artifact, changing both line citations and the substance of several app-patterns findings (fzf -> atuin re-references, SKILL.md citations) — editing the evidence a review node was meant to judge, owned by a still-provisional audit node. The judgment content that does exist (five-axis coherence analysis, roughness routed to candidate nodes 02-11) is genuinely useful and overlaps the design-review's 'weigh surfaces' spirit, which is why this is not a total fabrication — but it is framed and located as the wrong node's deliverable, skips the milestone-integration gate, and leaves the design-review's core outputs (per-finding dispositions, resolved Phase-2 set/order, concrete invariants) unproduced. That combination actively harms graph integrity (downstream gate artifact pre-populated; dependency skipped; upstream artifact mutated) and fails the node's intent, so the verdict is block with required human review. Lane-1 criteria adjudication is separate; this verdict stands on role preservation and graph integrity alone.
